idiom_name: static column-descriptor tables + offsetof over plain structs
implementation_notes: C has neither reflection nor an attribute mechanism, so the classic metadata mapping must be hand-built: keep entities as plain structs and declare one static descriptor array per type - {column name, offsetof(type, field), value type, size} - that a small generic mapper walks with sqlite3_column_* / PQgetvalue / prepared-statement bind calls. The field name appears once, in the descriptor, and never inside per-entity SQL. The structure is still justified for hand-written persistence layers over SQLite/PostgreSQL C APIs and in embedded targets where a full ORM is out of budget; X-macro generation or a small code generator normally replaces the manual upkeep of the descriptor whenever the schema is not tiny.
pitfalls: offsetof only works for standard-layout members: bit-fields and types with padding surprises make the descriptor silently wrong.
Nothing checks that the descriptor, the struct and the table agree - a renamed field compiles fine and fails at runtime (or writes to the wrong column).
Descriptor tables must be const/read-only and lazily built mapping caches need a lock, or concurrent initialisation races.
